texts: The heaviest wild tiger on record was a male Siberian (or Amur) tiger named "Radar." He weighed approximately 775 pounds (352 kilograms) when he was captured in the Russian Far East in 2017. Siberian tigers, also known as Amur tigers, are the largest subspecies of the Panthera genus, which also includes lions and jaguars. They can grow up to 10.5 feet (3.3 meters) in length and stand up to 4 feet (1.2 meters) tall at the shoulder. These massive cats are well-adapted to the cold climates of the Russian Far East and northeastern China, where they hunt large prey such as deer and wild boar. It's important to note that exact weight records can vary and Radar was an exceptional individual.

The heaviest wild tiger on record was an Amur (Siberian) tiger. It was a male and weighed a staggering 662 kilograms (1,463 pounds). This record-setting tiger was killed in the Russian Far East in 1950, and its weight was documented during the initial scientific research into the species in that region. Tigers are generally known for their incredible strength and power, though specific weights can vary significantly due to differences in habitat, diet, and individual genetics. Amur tigers are among the largest subspecies of tiger, with males typically weighing between 300 to 360 kg (661 to 795 lbs) in the wild.

The heaviest wild tiger on record is the Siberian tiger, with the record weight held by a male named Hannibal, who weighed approximately 680 pounds (308 kg) in 1956. However, it's important to note that their weights can vary greatly, and recent studies suggest that wild tigers can weigh even more. The largest tiger overall, considering all subspecies, was a male South China tiger named Mars, who was kept in captivity and weighed about 735 pounds (333 kg). In the wild, tigers typically weigh between 310 to 475 pounds (140 to 215 kg) for males and 230 to 310 pounds (104 to 140 kg) for females.

The largest reliably recorded wild tiger was a male Bengal tiger shot in northern India in 1967. It weighed 388.7 kg (857 pounds) and was documented in "The Guinness Book of Records." However, it's worth noting that there have been claims of larger tigers, but many of these lack proper documentation or verification. Generally, male Siberian (Amur) tigers are considered the largest tiger subspecies, with typical adult males weighing between 180-306 kg (397-674 pounds) in the wild, though they tend to be longer than Bengal tigers.
